missing_information_behavior: Do not suggest additional caffeine until habitual intake, source amounts, sleep and relevant health/medication context are clarified.
safety_exclusions: Do not treat 300 mg/day as a universal toxicity threshold.
Do not add event-linked caffeine on top of high baseline intake without individualized assessment.
Do not imply caffeine is suitable for every athlete or adult.
professional_escalation_conditions: Palpitations, arrhythmia, uncontrolled hypertension, panic symptoms, pregnancy or significant sleep disturbance.
Use of stimulant medicines or multiple caffeine-containing products.
population_and_context: Adults reporting high habitual caffeine intake; assess total caffeine from coffee, tea, energy drinks, pre-workout products and medicines before considering additional caffeine.
dose_constraints: No additional dose from this rule. Count total caffeine in mg/day and compare with life-stage- and jurisdiction-specific guidance; individual sensitivity varies.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance fact sheet discusses caffeine performance use and safety. Total exposure and individual tolerance matter; a single numeric threshold is not universally safe.
